entrypoints.summary: A malicious Wi-Fi or Ethernet network assigns the connected victim a public address and subnet that contains an attacker-selected Internet destination.
The test procedure configures an access point to hand out a public-address subnet containing the selected destination, then has the VPN-connected client request that destination.

observability.channel: Wireshark capture on the attacker-controlled local network
negative_controls: No plaintext TCP SYN to the selected public target appears on the local interface when the VPN routing invariant holds.
observability.positive_marker: Plaintext TCP SYN packet to the selected target; in some blocked cases, an ARP request for that target.

preconditions: Victim connects to an attacker-controlled Wi-Fi or Ethernet network.
The VPN client or platform configuration retains a local-network route exception that can apply to a publicly addressed local subnet.
Victim initiates traffic to a destination inside the attacker-advertised prefix.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A public IPv4 subnet/prefix that includes the chosen target IP, for example the test procedure’s target-containing 216.165.47.0/24 network.
trigger_steps.summary: Assign the victim a public-address subnet containing the target destination and have the victim enable or use the VPN.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: HTTP request or direct browser navigation to the selected target IP.
trigger_steps.summary: Cause a request to the selected destination and observe local-interface traffic.

sources.concept: malicious local network controlling client subnet assignment

impact.affected_asset: VPN confidentiality and routing isolation for traffic to selected public Internet destinations.
impact.attacker_capability: An adversary operating the victim’s connected local network can choose a public subnet covering a target and cause traffic for that target to be routed as local traffic.
impact.security_effect: Out-of-tunnel traffic leakage, with possible observation or interception of selected traffic; selected traffic can alternatively be blocked and local ARP requests can disclose attempted access.

causal_trace.summary: A local-network adversary controls the network addressing presented to a victim that connects to the adversary's Wi-Fi or Ethernet network, including a public subnet containing a chosen target address.

The advertised public prefix is treated as directly reachable local-network state, so the client’s exception that sends local traffic outside the tunnel applies to the selected public destination instead of the VPN default route.

When the victim requests the selected address, route selection emits packets on the local network outside the protected tunnel; the maintained procedure uses plaintext TCP SYN observation as the leakage indicator.

The local-network adversary can observe or intercept traffic sent to selected destinations outside the VPN; the same routing manipulation can also selectively block traffic, and ARP activity in blocking cases can reveal attempted visits.

failure.operation: Route a request for an attacker-selected public destination through the local interface under the local-network exception rather than through the VPN tunnel.

primary_invariant.statement: While the VPN is active, traffic to public Internet destinations must use the protected tunnel; a local-network exception must not exempt an attacker-selected public destination.
primary_invariant.violated_because: A malicious local network can advertise a public subnet containing the target, causing OS local-route treatment to take precedence over the VPN client’s default tunnel route.

quality.review_notes: This is a mechanism-level record, not a claim about any specific vendor revision. The paper and maintained procedure provide a concrete route/packet oracle, but the bundle contains neither vendor source nor patch diffs and no captured execution result for a particular client in this record. The test procedure establishes an oracle contract rather than a result from a run performed here.

remediation.invariant_restored: A public address advertised by the connected local network cannot cause traffic to that address to bypass the VPN tunnel via the local-network exception.
mitigation_classes: disable local-network access for public-address local networks
enforce that public-destination traffic remains tunnel-routed
use platform VPN APIs to include all networks while excluding local networks where applicable

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Operate a malicious Wi-Fi or Ethernet network and assign a public subnet containing the selected target address before the victim requests that target while VPN-connected.
data_structure_invariants: The VPN default route should cover public Internet destinations.
The local-network exception must not classify an attacker-selected public Internet target as exempt local traffic.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The adversary-selected prefix must contain the destination address targeted for leakage or blocking.
numeric_domains.name: advertised local subnet

state_context.state_machine: VPN inactive -> victim joins attacker-controlled local network and receives a target-containing public prefix -> VPN active with a default tunnel route plus local-network exception -> victim requests selected target -> local-route handling leaks or blocks the request.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: VPN clients and VPN/OS combinations evaluated in the USENIX Security 2023 TunnelCrack study; no per-vendor fixed or vulnerable version is asserted in this record.

target.component: VPN client operating-system routing-table configuration and local-network-access exception

oracle.channel: local-interface packet capture and routing behavior
oracle.expected_negative: A configuration that preserves the tunnel-routing invariant does not emit plaintext TCP SYN packets for the selected public target on the attacker-controlled local interface.
oracle.expected_positive: With a VPN-enabled client on an access point assigning a public subnet that contains the test target, plaintext TCP SYN packets to that target are observed on the local interface; ARP requests identify some blocked-but-locally-routed cases.
